overview: Both are repeated measurements to check reliability, but they test different sources of variation.
genZNote: Biological replicate: asking three different people the same question. Technical replicate: asking the same person the same question three times.

aspects.label: What Is Being Repeated
aspects.valueA: Independent biological samples (different animals, cultures, or individuals).
aspects.valueB: The same biological sample, measured multiple times using the same method.

aspects.label: Variation Captured
aspects.valueA: Captures true biological variability between subjects/samples.
aspects.valueB: Captures variability from the measurement/experimental process itself.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Measuring gene expression in three separate mice.
aspects.valueB: Measuring gene expression in the same mouse sample three times using the same assay.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: A well-designed experiment needs biological replicates to make any claim about a population — technical replicates alone can't tell you if a result generalises.
overlay.memoryTrick: Biological = different samples. Technical = same sample, repeated technique.
overlay.commonMisconception: Technical replicates cannot substitute for biological replicates — no amount of re-measuring one sample tells you whether the effect holds across individuals.
